methodology: The study employed the amino-yne reaction to achieve polymer-polymer conjugation and post-polymerization modification of amine-functional polymers. The reactions were conducted at room temperature without the use of any additives or catalysts.
research_objective: To extend the feasibility of the amino-yne reaction as a method for polymer-polymer conjugation and post-polymerization modification.

key_findings.finding: The amino-yne reaction was found to be effective for polymer-polymer conjugation and post-polymerization modification.
Poly(ethylene glycol) (mPEG-alkyne) can react with amine end-functional polymers such as polystyrene (PS-NH2) and poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM-NH2) to form block copolymers.

The amino-yne reaction can be used for the modification of amine-functional polymers like polyethylene imine and aminoethylaminopropylmethylsiloxane-dimethylsiloxane copolymer (poly(AEAPMS-co-DMS)) with quantitative or near-quantitative efficiency.
The amino-yne reaction can be classified under the term 'click chemistry' due to its simplicity and high efficiency.
The amino-yne reaction is reversible, forming an enamine bond that is often used in covalent adaptive network (CAN) structures.
Synthesis of functional propiolate esters and end-functional polymers using published procedures.
Polymer synthesis through esterification reaction between polyethylene glycol and pro- polic acid following a similar procedure described in the literature

However, this reaction has not been tested as a polymer-polymer conjugation Electron-deficient alkyne method and has also not been employed for post-polymerization modification (PPM) of amine-functional Polymer-polymer conjugation polymers. In this study, we aimed to extend the feasibility of amino-yne reactions using the aforementioned Post-polymerization modification strategies. For this purpose, for the first time, amine end-functional polymers, namely polystyrene (PS-NH2) and poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM-NH2), which were prepared experimentally or obtained commercially, were reacted with activated alkyne end-functional poly(ethylene glycol) (mPEG-alkyne) via amino-yne reaction to achieve the corresponding block copolymers, PNIPAM-b-PEG and PS-b-PEG. Both reactions proceeded at room temperature without the use of any additives or catalysts. Polymer-polymer conjugation reactions were found to be highly effective, as confirmed by GPC and 1H NMR analyses. The amino-yne reaction was then utilized for the modifications of two readily available amine-functional polymers: polyethylene imine (PEI) and aminoethylaminopropylmethylsiloxane-dimethylsiloxane copolymer (poly(AEAPMS-co-DMS)). These polymers were react cations of two readily available amine-functional polymers: polyethylene imine (PEI) and aminoethylaminopropylmethylsiloxane-dimethylsiloxane copolymer (poly(AEAPMS-co-DMS)). These polymers were reacted with various mono- and difunctional propiolate esters at room temperature for just two minutes. Experimental results show that both polymers could be modified with quantitative or near-quantitative effi- ciency, particularly with difunctional propiolates. We believe that this work has once again demonstrated the power of the amino-yne reaction, and this chemistry will definitely continue to attract interest among synthetic polymer chemists due to its rapid character, readily available starting materials, and mild conditions. 1.
